sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca hate duryodhane caiva hate sainye ca sarvaśaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājaḥ śrutvā kim akaron mune
english: Janamejaya said: When Duryodhana had been slain and the whole army utterly destroyed, what did the great king Dhṛtarāṣṭra do, O sage, on hearing of it?

sanskrit: tathaiva kauravo rājā dharmaputro mahāmanāḥ kṛpaprabhṛtayaś caiva kim akurvata te trayaḥ
english: And likewise the great-souled Kaurava king, the son of Dharma, and Kṛpa and the rest — what did those three do?

sanskrit: aśvatthāmnaḥ śrutaṃ karma śāpaś cānyonyakāritaḥ vṛttāntam uttaraṃ brūhi yad abhāṣata saṃjayaḥ
english: I have heard of Aśvatthāman's deed and of the mutual curse they pronounced upon one another; tell me what happened afterward — what Saṃjaya then related.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hate putraśate dīnaṃ chinnaśākham iva drumam putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahīpatim
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: With his hundred sons slain, the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra was wretched, like a tree whose branches have been lopped away, consumed by grief for his sons —

sanskrit: dhyānamūkatvam āpannaṃ cintayā samabhiplutam abhigamya mahāprājñaḥ saṃjayo vākyam abravīt
english: fallen mute in brooding, overwhelmed by sorrow; and the deeply wise Saṃjaya, approaching the lord of earth, spoke these words.

sanskrit: kiṃ śocasi mahārāja nāsti śoke sahāyatā akṣauhiṇyo hatāś cāṣṭau daśa caiva viśāṃ pate nirjaneyaṃ vasumatī śūnyā saṃprati kevalā
english: Why do you grieve, great king? There is no help in grief. Eighteen akṣauhiṇīs have been destroyed, O lord of peoples; this earth, rich in treasure, is now emptied of men, utterly desolate.

sanskrit: nānādigbhyaḥ samāgamya nānādeśyā narādhipāḥ sahitās tava putreṇa sarve vai nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: Kings from every quarter, men of many lands, gathered together with your son, and all alike have gone to their destruction.

sanskrit: pitṝṇāṃ putrapautrāṇāṃ jñātīnāṃ suhṛdāṃ tathā gurūṇāṃ cānupūrvyeṇa pretakāryāṇi kāraya
english: For your fathers, sons, and grandsons, your kinsmen and friends, and your elders, have the funeral rites performed, each in due order.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā karuṇaṃ vākyaṃ putrapautravadhārditaḥ papāta bhuvi durdharṣo vātāhata iva drumaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that piteous speech, the once-unassailable king, stricken by the slaughter of his sons and grandsons, fell to the earth like a tree struck down by the wind.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca hataputro hatāmātyo hatasarvasuhṛjjanaḥ duḥkhaṃ nūnaṃ bhaviṣyāmi vicaran pṛthivīm imām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: My sons slain, my counsellors slain, all my friends slain — surely I shall now wander this earth in misery.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu bandhuvihīnasya jīvitena mamādya vai lūnapakṣasya iva me jarājīrṇasya pakṣiṇaḥ
english: What use, now, is life to me, bereft of kinsmen — like a bird worn out by age, its wings shorn away?

sanskrit: hṛtarājyo hatasuhṛd dhatacakṣuś ca vai tathā na bhrājiṣye mahāprājña kṣīṇaraśmir ivāṃśumān
english: My kingdom taken, my friends slain, and my sight gone as well — I shall shine no more, O most wise one, like the sun whose rays have faded.

sanskrit: na kṛtaṃ suhṛdāṃ vākyaṃ jāmadagnyasya jalpataḥ nāradasya ca devarṣeḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanasya ca
english: I did not heed the words of my well-wishers — of Jāmadagnya as he spoke, of the divine sage Nārada, nor of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: sabhāmadhye tu kṛṣṇena yac chreyo 'bhihitaṃ mama alaṃ vaireṇa te rājan putraḥ saṃgṛhyatām iti
english: Nor what Kṛṣṇa, for my good, declared in the midst of the assembly: 'Enough of this enmity, O king; let your son be restrained.'

sanskrit: tac ca vākyam akṛtvāhaṃ bhṛśaṃ tapyāmi durmatiḥ na hi śrotāsmi bhīṣmasya dharmayuktaṃ prabhāṣitam
english: Having failed to act upon that counsel, I, the dull-witted one, now burn with bitter remorse; for I shall hear no more the righteous words spoken by Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: duryodhanasya ca tathā vṛṣabhasyeva nardataḥ duḥśāsanavadhaṃ śrutvā karṇasya ca viparyayam droṇasūryoparāgaṃ ca hṛdayaṃ me vidīryate
english: Recalling Duryodhana bellowing like a bull, and hearing of the slaying of Duḥśāsana, of the overthrow of Karṇa, and of the eclipse of that sun which was Droṇa — my heart is torn asunder.

sanskrit: na smarāmy ātmanaḥ kiṃ cit purā saṃjaya duṣkṛtam yasyedaṃ phalam adyeha mayā mūḍhena bhujyate
english: I cannot recall, Saṃjaya, any misdeed of mine in the past whose fruit it is that I, the deluded one, now reap here today.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ hy apakṛtaṃ kiṃ cin mayā pūrveṣu janmasu yena māṃ duḥkhabhāgeṣu dhātā karmasu yuktavān
english: Surely some wrong was done by me in former births, that the Ordainer has yoked me to deeds whose lot is sorrow.

sanskrit: pariṇāmaś ca vayasaḥ sarvabandhukṣayaś ca me suhṛnmitravināśaś ca daivayogād upāgataḥ ko 'nyo 'sti duḥkhitataro mayā loke pumān iha
english: The decline of my years, the loss of all my kinsmen, and the destruction of my friends and allies have come upon me through the working of fate. Who else in this world is a man more wretched than I?

sanskrit: tan mām adyaiva paśyantu pāṇḍavāḥ saṃśitavratam vivṛtaṃ brahmalokasya dīrgham adhvānam āsthitam
english: Therefore let the Pāṇḍavas behold me this very day, firm in a stern vow, set upon the long road that lies open to the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya lālapyamānasya bahuśokaṃ vicinvataḥ śokāpahaṃ narendrasya saṃjayo vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the lord of men lamented thus, dwelling on his many sorrows, Saṃjaya spoke words to dispel that grief.

sanskrit: śokaṃ rājan vyapanuda śrutās te vedaniścayāḥ śāstrāgamāś ca vividhā vṛddhebhyo nṛpasattama sṛñjaye putraśokārte yad ūcur munayaḥ purā
english: Cast off your grief, O king. You have heard the settled truths of the Vedas and the various teachings of the scriptures from the elders, O best of kings — what the sages once said to Sṛñjaya when he was stricken with grief for his son.

sanskrit: tathā yauvanajaṃ darpam āsthite te sute nṛpa na tvayā suhṛdāṃ vākyaṃ bruvatām avadhāritam svārthaś ca na kṛtaḥ kaś cil lubdhena phalagṛddhinā
english: When your son had given himself over to the arrogance born of youth, you did not heed the words of your friends as they spoke; nor did you, greedy and hungry for gain, pursue any true good of your own.

sanskrit: tava duḥśāsano mantrī rādheyaś ca durātmavān śakuniś caiva duṣṭātmā citrasenaś ca durmatiḥ śalyaś ca yena vai sarvaṃ śalyabhūtaṃ kṛtaṃ jagat
english: Your counsellors were Duḥśāsana and the wicked-souled Rādheya, the evil-natured Śakuni, the ill-minded Citrasena, and Śalya — by whom the whole world was turned into a thorn of affliction.

sanskrit: kuruvṛddhasya bhīṣmasya gāndhāryā vidurasya ca na kṛtaṃ vacanaṃ tena tava putreṇa bhārata
english: The word of Bhīṣma, the elder of the Kurus, and of Gāndhārī and Vidura was not heeded by that son of yours, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: na dharmaḥ satkṛtaḥ kaś cin nityaṃ yuddham iti bruvan kṣapitāḥ kṣatriyāḥ sarve śatrūṇāṃ vardhitaṃ yaśaḥ
english: No righteousness was ever honored by him; crying always 'War! War!', he destroyed all the kṣatriyas and increased the glory of his foes.

sanskrit: madhyastho hi tvam apy āsīr na kṣamaṃ kiṃ cid uktavān dhūr dhareṇa tvayā bhāras tulayā na samaṃ dhṛtaḥ
english: And you yourself stood neutral, saying nothing that befitted the case; you who should have borne the yoke did not hold the burden level in the balance.

sanskrit: ādāv eva manuṣyeṇa vartitavyaṃ yathā kṣamam yathā nātītam arthaṃ vai paścāttāpena yujyate
english: From the very outset a man must act as is fitting, so that he be not afflicted with remorse over a matter once it has passed beyond recall.

sanskrit: putragṛddhyā tvayā rājan priyaṃ tasya cikīrṣatā paścāttāpam idaṃ prāptaṃ na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: Through fondness for your son, O king, and a wish to do what pleased him, you have come to this remorse; you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: madhu yaḥ kevalaṃ dṛṣṭvā prapātaṃ nānupaśyati sa bhraṣṭo madhulobhena śocaty eva yathā bhavān
english: He who, seeing only the honey, does not perceive the precipice beyond, is brought to ruin by his greed for the honey and grieves — even as you do.

sanskrit: arthān na śocan prāpnoti na śocan vindate sukham na śocañ śriyam āpnoti na śocan vindate param
english: Not by grieving does one gain wealth; not by grieving does one find happiness; not by grieving does one attain fortune; not by grieving does one win the supreme.

sanskrit: svayam utpādayitvāgniṃ vastreṇa pariveṣṭayet dahyamāno manastāpaṃ bhajate na sa paṇḍitaḥ
english: A man who, having himself kindled a fire, then wraps himself in cloth, and as he burns gives way to anguish of mind — such a one is no wise man.

sanskrit: tvayaiva sasutenāyaṃ vākyavāyusamīritaḥ lobhājyena ca saṃsikto jvalitaḥ pārthapāvakaḥ
english: It was by you and your son that this fire which is Pārtha was fanned by the wind of words, drenched with the clarified butter of greed, and set ablaze.

sanskrit: tasmin samiddhe patitāḥ śalabhā iva te sutāḥ tān keśavārcir nirdagdhān na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: Into that blaze your sons fell like moths; consumed by the flame that was Keśava, they are gone — and you ought not to grieve for them.

sanskrit: yac cāśrupātakalilaṃ vadanaṃ vahase nṛpa aśāstradṛṣṭam etad dhi na praśaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ
english: And this face you bear, sullied with falling tears, O king — this the wise do not commend, for it is not sanctioned by the scriptures.

sanskrit: visphuliṅgā iva hy etān dahanti kila mānavān jahīhi manyuṃ buddhyā vai dhārayātmānam ātmanā
english: These tears, they say, scorch men like sparks of fire. Cast off your anguish through wisdom; uphold the self by the self.

sanskrit: evam āśvāsitas tena saṃjayena mahātmanā viduro bhūya evāha buddhipūrvaṃ paraṃtapa
english: Thus consoled by the great-souled Saṃjaya, Vidura in turn spoke further, with thoughtful counsel, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'mṛtasamair vākyair hlādayan puruṣarṣabham vaicitravīryaṃ viduro yad uvāca nibodha tat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, gladdening that bull among men, the son of Vicitravīrya, with words like nectar, Vidura spoke — hear now what he said.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca uttiṣṭha rājan kiṃ śeṣe dhārayātmānam ātmanā sthirajaṅgamamartyānāṃ sarveṣām eṣa nirṇayaḥ
english: Vidura said: Rise up, O king! Why do you lie there? Uphold the self by the self. This is the appointed end of all that is fixed and moving and mortal.

sanskrit: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam
english: All hoardings end in loss, all that rises ends in a fall; unions end in separation, and life itself ends in death.

sanskrit: yadā śūraṃ ca bhīruṃ ca yamaḥ karṣati bhārata tat kiṃ na yotsyanti hi te kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabha
english: When Yama drags off the brave man and the coward alike, O descendant of Bharata, then why should those kṣatriyas not have fought, O bull among kṣatriyas?

sanskrit: ayudhyamāno mriyate yudhyamānaś ca jīvati kālaṃ prāpya mahārāja na kaś cid ativartate
english: He who does not fight dies, and he who fights lives on; but when his hour has come, O great king, no one passes beyond it.

sanskrit: na cāpy etān hatān yuddhe rājañ śocitum arhasi pramāṇaṃ yadi śāstrāṇi gatās te paramāṃ gatim
english: Nor ought you to grieve, O king, for these slain in battle; if the scriptures are our authority, they have attained the supreme goal.

sanskrit: sarve svādhyāyavanto hi sarve ca caritavratāḥ sarve cābhimukhāḥ kṣīṇās tatra kā paridevanā
english: All of them were men of sacred study, all had fulfilled their vows, and all fell facing the foe — what cause for lamentation is there in that?

sanskrit: adarśanād āpatitāḥ punaś cādarśanaṃ gatāḥ na te tava na teṣāṃ tvaṃ tatra kā paridevanā
english: Out of the unseen they came forth, and to the unseen they have returned again; they are not yours, nor are you theirs — what cause for lamentation is there?

sanskrit: hato 'pi labhate svargaṃ hatvā ca labhate yaśaḥ ubhayaṃ no bahuguṇaṃ nāsti niṣphalatā raṇe
english: Slain, one wins heaven; slaying, one wins glory. Both, indeed, are of great worth to us; there is no fruitlessness in battle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kāmadughāṃl lokān indraḥ saṃkalpayiṣyati indrasyātithayo hy ete bhavanti puruṣarṣabha
english: Indra will ordain for them worlds that grant every wish; for these become the guests of Indra, O bull among men.

sanskrit: na yajñair dakṣiṇāvadbhir na tapobhir na vidyayā svargaṃ yānti tathā martyā yathā śūrā raṇe hatāḥ
english: Not by sacrifices rich in gifts, nor by austerities, nor by sacred learning do mortals go to heaven as do heroes slain in battle.

sanskrit: mātāpitṛsahasrāṇi putradāraśatāni ca saṃsāreṣv anubhūtāni kasya te kasya vā vayam
english: Thousands of mothers and fathers, and hundreds of sons and wives, have been known in the rounds of existence — whose are they, or whose are we?

sanskrit: śokasthānasahasrāṇi bhayasthānaśatāni ca divase divase mūḍham āviśanti na paṇḍitam
english: Thousands of occasions for grief and hundreds for fear assail the deluded man day after day, but not the wise.

sanskrit: na kālasya priyaḥ kaś cin na dveṣyaḥ kurusattama na madhyasthaḥ kva cit kālaḥ sarvaṃ kālaḥ prakarṣati
english: To Time none is dear and none is hateful, O best of the Kurus; Time is nowhere neutral — Time drags all things away.

sanskrit: anityaṃ jīvitaṃ rūpaṃ yauvanaṃ dravyasaṃcayaḥ ārogyaṃ priyasaṃvāso gṛdhyed eṣu na paṇḍitaḥ
english: Life is fleeting, and so are beauty, youth, the hoarding of goods, health, and the company of loved ones; the wise man does not crave after these.

sanskrit: na jānapadikaṃ duḥkham ekaḥ śocitum arhasi apy abhāvena yujyeta tac cāsya na nivartate
english: You ought not to grieve alone over a sorrow that belongs to a whole realm; though one might even perish by it, the calamity is not thereby turned back.

sanskrit: aśocan pratikurvīta yadi paśyet parākramam bhaiṣajyam etad duḥkhasya yad etan nānucintayet cintyamānaṃ hi na vyeti bhūyaś cāpi vivardhate
english: If one sees a way to act, let him counter the trouble without grieving; but the remedy for sorrow is not to brood upon it — for the sorrow that is dwelt upon does not depart, and instead grows the greater.

sanskrit: aniṣṭasaṃprayogāc ca viprayogāt priyasya ca manuṣyā mānasair duḥkhair yujyante ye 'lpabuddhayaḥ
english: From union with the unwished-for and from separation from the dear, men of little understanding are yoked to sorrows of the mind.

sanskrit: nārtho na dharmo na sukhaṃ yad etad anuśocasi na ca nāpaiti kāryārthāt trivargāc caiva bhraśyate
english: This over which you grieve is neither gain nor righteousness nor happiness; the grief does not depart from the purpose of any deed, and through it one falls away from the threefold aim of life.

sanskrit: anyām anyāṃ dhanāvasthāṃ prāpya vaiśeṣikīṃ narāḥ asaṃtuṣṭāḥ pramuhyanti saṃtoṣaṃ yānti paṇḍitāḥ
english: Attaining one richer state of wealth after another, men remain unsatisfied and are bewildered; but the wise come to contentment.

sanskrit: prajñayā mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ hanyāc chārīram auṣadhaiḥ etaj jñānasya sāmarthyaṃ na bālaiḥ samatām iyāt
english: Mental suffering one should slay with wisdom, and bodily suffering with medicines; this is the power of knowledge — let one not in this become the equal of fools.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ cānuśayati tiṣṭhantaṃ cānutiṣṭhati anudhāvati dhāvantaṃ karma pūrvakṛtaṃ naram
english: As a man lies down, the deed once done lies down with him; as he stands, it stands with him; and as he runs, it runs after him.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ yasyām avasthāyāṃ yat karoti śubhāśubham tasyāṃ tasyām avasthāyāṃ tat tat phalam upāśnute
english: In whatever condition a man does a deed, good or evil, in that very condition he reaps the fruit thereof.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca subhāṣitair mahāprājña śoko 'yaṃ vigato mama bhuya eva tu vākyāni śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: By your well-spoken words, O most wise one, this grief of mine has passed away; yet I wish to hear your words once more, in their truth.

sanskrit: aniṣṭānāṃ ca saṃsargād iṣṭānāṃ ca vivarjanāt kathaṃ hi mānasair duḥkhaiḥ pramucyante 'tra paṇḍitāḥ
english: From contact with the unwished-for and from the loss of the cherished, how is it that the wise are here freed from sorrows of the mind?

sanskrit: vidura uvāca yato yato mano duḥkhāt sukhād vāpi pramucyate tatas tataḥ śamaṃ labdhvā sugatiṃ vindate budhaḥ
english: Vidura said: From whatever source the mind is freed, whether from pain or from pleasure, from each such source the wise man, having gained peace, attains a happy state.

sanskrit: aśāśvatam idaṃ sarvaṃ cintyamānaṃ nararṣabha kadalīsaṃnibho lokaḥ sāro hy asya na vidyate
english: When pondered, all this is impermanent, O bull among men; the world is like the plantain tree — no pith of it is to be found.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇy eva hi martyānām āhur dehāni paṇḍitāḥ kālena viniyujyante sattvam ekaṃ tu śobhanam
english: The wise declare the bodies of mortals to be but dwellings; in time they are cast off, and the spirit alone is the abiding good.

sanskrit: yathā jīrṇam ajīrṇaṃ vā vastraṃ tyaktvā tu vai naraḥ anyad rocayate vastram evaṃ dehāḥ śarīriṇām
english: As a man, casting off a garment whether worn out or not, chooses another garment, so are the bodies of embodied beings.

sanskrit: vaicitravīrya vāsaṃ hi duḥkhaṃ vā yadi vā sukham prāpnuvantīha bhūtāni svakṛtenaiva karmaṇā
english: O son of Vicitravīrya, whether a sojourn be of sorrow or of joy, beings here attain it through the deeds they themselves have wrought.

sanskrit: karmaṇā prāpyate svargaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca bhārata tato vahati taṃ bhāram avaśaḥ svavaśo 'pi vā
english: By one's deeds are heaven, pleasure, and pain attained, O descendant of Bharata; and so each bears that burden, whether helplessly or of his own will.

sanskrit: yathā ca mṛnmayaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ cakrārūḍhaṃ vipadyate kiṃ cit prakriyamāṇaṃ vā kṛtamātram athāpi vā
english: And as an earthen vessel set upon the wheel may perish — some while still being shaped, or others just when made —

sanskrit: chinnaṃ vāpy avaropyantam avatīrṇam athāpi vā ārdraṃ vāpy atha vā śuṣkaṃ pacyamānam athāpi vā
english: or when cut from the wheel, or being lifted off, or already taken down; while still moist, or dried, or being fired in the kiln —

sanskrit: avatāryamāṇam āpākād uddhṛtaṃ vāpi bhārata atha vā paribhujyantam evaṃ dehāḥ śarīriṇām
english: or being drawn out of the kiln, or already taken up, or even while in use, O descendant of Bharata — so it is with the bodies of embodied beings.

sanskrit: garbhastho vā prasūto vāpy atha vā divasāntaraḥ ardhamāsagato vāpi māsamātragato 'pi vā
english: Still in the womb, or newly born, or but a day old, or come to half a month, or grown to a month alone —

sanskrit: saṃvatsaragato vāpi dvisaṃvatsara eva vā yauvanastho 'pi madhyastho vṛddho vāpi vipadyate
english: or come to a year, or to a second year, in the bloom of youth, in middle age, or in old age — a man perishes.

sanskrit: prākkarmabhis tu bhūtāni bhavanti na bhavanti ca evaṃ sāṃsiddhike loke kimartham anutapyase
english: By the deeds of former lives beings come into being and pass away; in a world so ordered by necessity, to what end do you grieve?

sanskrit: yathā ca salile rājan krīḍārtham anusaṃcaran unmajjec ca nimajjec ca kiṃ cit sattvaṃ narādhipa
english: And as in the water, O king, some creature roaming about in play may rise and may sink again, O lord of men —

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃsāragahanād unmajjananimajjanāt karmabhogena badhyantaḥ kliśyante ye 'lpabuddhayaḥ
english: even so, from the thicket of worldly existence, in the rising and the sinking, those of little understanding are bound by the reaping of their deeds and are tormented.

sanskrit: ye tu prājñāḥ sthitāḥ satye saṃsārāntagaveṣiṇaḥ samāgamajñā bhūtānāṃ te yānti paramāṃ gatim
english: But those who are wise, established in truth, seeking the end of worldly existence, who know the way beings come together — they attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ saṃsāragahanaṃ vijñeyaṃ vadatāṃ vara etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tattvam ākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How is the thicket of worldly existence to be understood, O best of speakers? This I wish to hear; tell me the truth of it, for I ask.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca janmaprabhṛti bhūtānāṃ kriyāḥ sarvāḥ śṛṇu prabho pūrvam eveha kalale vasate kiṃ cid antaram
english: Vidura said: Hear, O lord, all the workings of beings from birth onward. At first the embryo dwells here in the fluid stage for a certain interval.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pañcame 'tīte māse māṃsaṃ prakalpayet tataḥ sarvāṅgasaṃpūrṇo garbho māse prajāyate
english: Then, when the fifth month has passed, it takes on flesh; and thereafter, with all its limbs complete, the child is born in due month.
